transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Ortiz (Redwood) — Priya Nair, Ethan Cole, Liam Brooks (Valora)

Summary: quick posture inventory + walk through of Trust Center. conversation about keys and who holds them, and how logs are exported for audits.

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. we've got Daniel here to handle the tech detail.
[00:14] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. We're trying to get a clean map of what evidence you'll hand over for our SOC 2/ISO audit and how we can access it in the Trust Center. Also want to cover KMS patterns if we go with private/dedicated.
[00:28] Daniel: Great, thanks Priya. quick agenda: 1) reports and scope, 2) trustcenter access + evidence export, 3) KMS + BYOK options, 4) logs and retention. sound ok?
[00:39] Ethan: yes that works. I'll be tracking the network/KMS bits.
[00:46] Liam: And I'll focus on logging and SIEM integration.
[00:51] Maya: Perfect. quick housekeeping — call is being recorded, we'll share notes.

[03:05] Daniel: So first, SOC 2. Redwood has a Type II for the hosted service, our scope includes the inference API endpoints, Console access, and Trust Center for evidence. the PDF is the formal artifact. note: our dedicated and private offerings have separate attestations depending on where the control boundary is drawn.
[03:36] Priya: when you say "separate attestations" do you mean customers who deploy private will be responsible for certain controls?
[03:44] Daniel: yes, exactly. for private/on-prem the customer controls parts of infra — so our report notes shared responsibility sections.
[03:55] Priya: ok good to know. we'll need that mapping for our audit.

[06:12] Maya: we'll send the SOC2 PDF and a control mapping doc that lists which controls are Redwood's and which ones are Valora's. it's usually a table but we'll include notes for Private versus Dedicated.
[06:28] Priya: good. and ISO 27001? scope and certification posture?
[06:34] Daniel: Redwood maintains ISO-aligned processes and we maintain an ISO artefact set for the platform — it's not a single certificate for every customer, but we provide the evidence index and control alignment. for customers requiring ISO cert as part of procurement we produce a scope matrix.
[06:54] Ethan: would that include any explicit network diagrams showing VPC peering?
[07:02] Daniel: not full network diagrams by default for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we can provide the topology templates and a sample peering diagram. we can also coordinate a short tech call to walk through your exact topology.

[10:15] Liam: earlier I mentioned logs — what does the Trust Center export look like? can we get raw audit logs or only high-level artifacts?
[10:28] Daniel: Trust Center exposes both pre-packaged evidence (screenshots, configs) and raw logs for certain types. for audit purposes we can provide S3-exportable bundles (redacted) and access controls to let your auditors read-only. retention periods vary by offering — default 90 days in hosted but Dedicated can be configured for longer.
[10:55] Priya: 90 days is too short for us, our policy is 12 months for infra logs.
[11:03] Daniel: understood — on Dedicated we can push retention to 12 months; for Private you control retention fully.

[13:20] Ethan: KMS question — if we want BYOK, where do keys live? are they in Redwood-managed KMS or do we bring our own keys?
[13:34] Daniel: we support a BYOK workflow. three patterns: 1) Redwood-managed KMS (default) 2) Customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK) with remote CMKs 3) HSM/BYOK where keys never leave customer's HSM (on-prem or cloud). for the last two, some controls shift to the customer and we document the handoff.
[13:59] Priya: can you show the key flow? how is the envelope encryption handled?
[14:07] Daniel: sure — high level: model artifacts are encrypted at rest with a data encryption key (DEK), DEK is wrapped by a KMS CMK. if you bring CMK, Redwood will store wrapped keys but the CMK policy controls unwrap. in BYOK/HSM cases we provide a diagram. I'll attach the diagram in follow-up.

[17:45] Liam: any latency implications if we use customer-managed KMS? we can't have large token overheads on every inference call.
[17:56] Daniel: good point. our runtime caches unwrapped DEKs and rotates them per policy, so per-token latency impact is minimal. there's an initial unwrap cost on startup and occasional re-wraps. for high throughput we recommend Dedicated with local KMS endpoints.

[21:10] Priya: about evidence access — can auditors log into Trust Center directly or do they receive an export?
[21:20] Maya: both options. we can create temporary auditor accounts with time-limited SSO and read-only role, or we can provide exported bundles. customer preference.
[21:31] Ethan: we prefer exported immutable bundles, but a quick Trust Center session would help to validate gaps.

[24:02] Daniel: quick note on controls mapping — we'll produce a CSV with control id, description, owner (Redwood/Customer), artifact path in Trust Center, and example evidence. that should speed your audit team's work.
[24:18] Priya: perfect. do you also provide raw config snapshots for things like IAM roles and access lists?
[24:27] Daniel: yes, for Dedicated/Private we can provide IAM snapshots and sample Terraform states; for hosted we provide screenshots and exported role lists.

[28:05] Liam: regarding SIEM integration — can we push audit logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
[28:15] Daniel: yes, we support push/export via S3 or direct log forwarders; for Dedicated we can set up VPC peering to forward logs to your collector.
[28:30] Ethan: do you preserve request-level user identifiers in logs or are they pseudonymized?
[28:38] Daniel: our default is pseudonymized request ids for hosted to protect PII; Dedicated/Private can be configured to include user principal if you need that for traceability, subject to privacy regs.

[32:50] Priya: data residency — our requirement is that inference data stays in EU regions. can Redwood pin workloads?
[33:02] Maya: yes, we support region pinning. for dedicated pools or private deployments you can pin the model serving region. for hosted we have region controls and can route traffic to a specific region but note replication/backups may vary. we'll provide the region-residency SLA notes.

[36:12] Ethan: one gap I noticed — for on-prem BYOK we need clarity on the attestation around key custody. do you provide evidence that the keys never left customer's HSM?
[36:22] Daniel: we can provide logs of key unwrap calls and KMS audit trails that show operations, plus an architecture diagram. for absolute proof, customers often request an HSM certificate from the provider; we can coordinate with your security team on the exact artifacts.

[40:00] Priya: procurement will also ask for data flow diagrams showing where PII touches the stack. do you have a redacted PII flow?
[40:12] Maya: yes we'll include a redacted data flow and the default privacy safeguards. note that Redwood's default is to not persist user inputs longer than needed, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention.

[43:30] Daniel: one thing to flag: if you opt for Dedicated with BYOK there's an operational runbook we'll supply for KMS rotation and breach-response roles. that runbook is part of our enterprise onboarding.
[43:46] Liam: can we get the runbook?
[43:49] Maya: yes — action item: Daniel will share runbook extract.

[47:15] Ethan: small nit — who will be the contact for evidence delivery during the audit window? we want a single POC.
[47:24] Maya: Maya will be the account POC for procurement & legal; Daniel is technical POC for evidence exports.

[50:05] Priya: timeline — our audit window is late May. we need to finalize controls mapping by mid April.
[50:14] Maya: ok we'll aim to deliver mapping by 2027-03-24 so you have time to review.

[52:30] Daniel: quick demo of Trust Center (brief): (screen share audio) — you can see the evidence index, search, and download buttons. note: the export zips are redacted by default — we can toggle levels.
[55:10] Priya: looks straightforward. two follow ups: 1) include a note about log hashing and chain-of-custody in the export; 2) confirm retention configuration for Dedicated.
[55:30] Daniel: noted. we'll include chain-of-custody hashes in the exported bundle and confirm retention settings for Dedicated in writing.

[57:00] Maya: recap — we'll send SOC2 + ISO index, control mapping CSV, Trust Center read-only link or export options, KMS flow diagram and runbook extract. Daniel will set up the network/topology follow-up. Ethan will confirm regions. Priya will feed back any mandatory artifacts from procurement.
[57:20] Priya: thanks everyone, that's helpful.
[57:30] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up by email with the artifacts and set the topology call. Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional mis-transcriptions in the recording: "Trust Center" sometimes captured as "trust center", some names mis-attributed in automated labels.
